# Results

## Free generation: article flips co-occur with noun-token changes

Amplifying frozen dual-effect features on 20 held-out prompts moves
article preference toward `an` on every prompt, but almost never
preserves the baseline noun token. Concrete twins include
`a pilot`\(\rightarrow\)`an aviator`,
`a lawyer`\(\rightarrow\)`an attorney`, and
`a physicist`\(\rightarrow\)`an astronomer`.
@tbl-packaging reports rates: package-like switches dominate
(0.95; 95\% Clopper--Pearson interval comfortably above chance);
wrapper-like repairs are \(0/20\) (upper 95\% bound \(\approx 0.17\));
illicit `an`+consonant mismatches stay at zero. Matched controls do not
reproduce the package-like switch. Column ``\(\Delta\) art.\ logit favors
`an`'' is a *logit-direction* readout and need not equal a generated-article
switch (hence the control can score 0.70 there while preserving the noun
token and scoring 0.00 wrapper-like).

| Condition | \(N\) | \(\Delta\) art.\ logit favors `an` | Noun token preserved | Class shift | Wrapper-like | Package-like | Twin match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 1.00 | 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.00 | 0.95 | 0.35 |
| S1 matched control | 20 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| S3 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 0.70 | 0.95 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.00 |

: Free-generation metrics (held-out occupations). S1 is dual-effect; S3 is
content-ish. Wrapper-like = generated article moves and noun token stays;
package-like = legal article--class switch.
{#tbl-packaging}

An earlier frozen LoF pair that repaired the source mismatch
`a ophthalmologist`\(\rightarrow\)`an ophthalmologist` likewise failed as
a noun-preserving transfer: on held-out data it flipped many
expected-`a` controls toward `an` and changed noun tokens on 37/107
prompts, with **zero** grammar-only repairs that kept the noun fixed
(@fig-generalization; bridge details in Appendix~A).

![Held-out frozen-pair transfer changes articles and noun tokens together rather than repairing grammar alone.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure3_generalization.png){#fig-generalization width=82%}

## Selection rule and dose do not open a wrapper window

Changing how features are selected does not yield noun-preserving article
edits (@fig-selection). Across S1--S4 at \(5\times\) amplify, wrapper-like
rate is \(0/20\) in each arm. Only S1 is strongly package-like (0.95);
S2/S3 stay near 0.05; S4 (competing `a`) produces neither wrappers nor
`an`-packages under amplification. Dual-effect selection therefore
matters for free-generation package-like behavior, but does not by itself
identify a fused latent package (**H2**) versus article-driven
continuation (**H3**).

![No selection rule yields held-out wrapper-like repair; dual-effect S1 is almost purely package-like.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure4_selection_ablation.png){#fig-selection width=78%}

A dose sweep on S1 likewise finds **no wrapper window**
(@fig-dose). As gain rises from \(1.5\times\) to \(8\times\), noun-token
preservation falls from 0.90 to 0.05 while package-like rate rises from
0.10 to 0.95; wrapper-like rate remains 0.00 at every point. Mild doses
mostly do little; stronger doses buy package-like switches, not
grammar-only edits.

![Dose–response for dual-effect features: package-like rate rises with gain; wrapper-like rate stays at zero.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure5_dose_response.png){#fig-dose width=78%}

## Dual lock and twin tetrad: coordinated outputs under free generation

If modular planning existed as an editable wrapper, amplifying
article-moving features while locking content-supporting features should
raise wrapper-like success above article-push alone. Under free
generation it does not (@fig-dual): content-lock alone (S3) preserves
noun tokens (\(\approx 0.95\)) but barely moves articles; article-push
(S1) and dual S1+S3 both remain \(\approx 95\%\) package-like with
wrapper-like and illicit mismatch rates at 0.00. Completions re-bundle
into legal pairs (`an aviator`, `an attorney`) rather than `an`+`pilot`.

![Content-lock preserves noun tokens but does not move articles; dual intervention still class-switches into legal pairs.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure6_dual_lock.png){#fig-dual width=82%}

On pre-specified twins, a causal tetrad shows sufficiency and specificity
of free-generation package-like selection relative to matched controls
(@fig-tetrad): baseline and LoF (zero S1) remain `a pilot` / `a lawyer`;
GoF (amplify S1) selects `an aviator` / `an attorney`; control amplify
does not. This establishes controllable *output* coordination under free
generation; it does not identify the internal representation as a fused
package.

![Gain-of-function selects the vowel-initial twin completion; matched random amplifications do not.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure7_causal_tetrad.png){#fig-tetrad width=82%}

## Pasting native \(b\) restores the native noun token

Under selective article-step intervention with clamps **off** at the noun
step, free S1 amplify remains package-like (\(\approx 95\%\)), but forcing
the native article yields noun-token preservation \(\approx 1.0\): e.g.,
free `an aviator` becomes `a pilot` after pasting `a`
(@fig-force-native). This is exactly what **H3** predicts if noun-token
changes are mediated by the generated article. It isolates a real
\(b\to c\) path. It does **not** yet measure a controlled direct effect of
the intervention on \(c\), because content clamps were absent at \(c\).

![Free dual-effect intervention switches article--noun completions; pasting the native article restores the native noun token.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure8_selective_force_native.png){#fig-force-native width=88%}

## Fixed \(b\), intervention on: little behavioral noun-token control

@tbl-fixed-b and @fig-fixed-b report the corrected assay. Across eight
occupation families, S3 amplify (\(5\times\)/\(8\times\)), S3 zero,
hint-contrast amplify, and matched controls yield **zero** within-class
top-1 noun switches under fixed native \(b\) with interventions kept on at
\(P\) (\(0/8\); Clopper--Pearson 95\% upper bound \(\approx 0.37\)).
Same-class noun logits typically remain \(\approx 5\) below the source
noun---a severe **floor**: a real target-specific effect of a few tenths
of a logit would rarely flip top-1. Protocol smoke tests confirm
intervention-on versus off differ somewhere in the logits, but that does
not validate target-specific transmission.

| Condition | Top-1 within-class switch | Noun token \(\Delta\) | Match same-class | Mean \(\Delta\)(same$-$src) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.90\) |
| S3 amp \(5\times\) / \(8\times\) / zero | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(\approx -4.9\) |
| Hint-contrast amp \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.91\) |
| Control amp \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.92\) |

: Fixed-\(b\), intervention-on-at-\(c\) rates (8 families). Top-1 zeros are
not decisive given \(\approx 5\)-logit floors and small \(N\).
{#tbl-fixed-b}

![Corrected fixed-\(b\) assay: binary within-class top-1 outcomes are zero; same-class nouns stay ~5 logits below source.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure9_fixed_b_content_on.png){#fig-fixed-b width=80%}

## Additional handles, near-boundary pairs, and a failed positive control

A modular reading might blame the wrong sparse objects. We therefore
also tested Latent-Planning-style per-example features and a dense MLP-in
hint-contrast direction under the same fixed-\(b\) schedule on three twin
families (@tbl-handles; @fig-residual). Top-1 within-class switches remain
\(0/3\) (upper 95\% bound \(\approx 0.71\)). Best continuous
same$-$source improvements are tiny (\(+0.29\) logits for per-noun;
\(\approx +0.08\) for residual content), and the residual content
direction does **not** beat matched-norm random controls
(\(\approx +0.15\)). Every force-on continuation remained on the baseline
noun token.

![Dense residual (MLP-in) content steering under fixed \(b\): within-class top-1 outcomes remain zero for content and random directions.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure11_residual_fixed_b.png){#fig-residual width=82%}

| Handle | Best top-1 \(c\to c\) | Best \(\Delta\Delta\)(same$-$src) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Per-noun LP-target / contrast (amp \(5\times\)--\(8\times\)) | 0.00 | \(+0.29\) |
| Residual content steer \(\alpha=1\)--\(8\) | 0.00 | \(\approx 0.08\) |
| Residual random control \(\alpha=1\)--\(8\) | 0.00 | \(\approx 0.15\) |

: Additional fixed-\(b\) handles. Neither per-noun sparse selection nor
residual MLP-in steering opens a within-class top-1 dial; residual content
steering does not beat random controls.
{#tbl-handles}

To address floor effects we screened 12 same-article-class occupation
pairs for baseline target$-$source gaps under fixed native \(b\). Two pairs
are near-boundary (`scientist`/`biologist` at \(-0.75\) logits;
`scientist`/`chemist` at \(-1.13\)). As a **positive control**, we then
ran oracle MLP-in activation patching
\((1-\lambda)\mathrm{act}_{\mathrm{source}}+\lambda\mathrm{act}_{\mathrm{target}}\)
at layers \(\{8,10,12,14\}\) under fixed \(b\), versus matched-norm random
patches (5 seeds). Across four test pairs and \(\lambda\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75,1\}\),
oracle top-1 target matches were \(0/4\) per mix (upper 95\% bound
\(\approx 0.60\)); mean \(\Delta\Delta\) stayed within
\(\approx 0.03\)--\(0.06\) logits and did not clearly separate from random
controls (Appendix E). Thus this oracle construction **does not validate**
that the fixed-\(b\) protocol can transmit behaviorally sufficient
noun-token control at these sites. We therefore treat fixed-\(b\) top-1
nulls as evidence about **tested handles under floor-limited targets**,
not as proof that no independent noun pathway exists.
